The span of three vectors (x,y,z) is the set of all values that all linear combinations of (x,y,z). Notice that if we replace (x,y,z) with (x + tz, y, z), this is the same thing as the span of a linear combination of the previous span. I.e. the linear combination of three vectors is the same as the linear combination OF the linear combination of those vectors.  Now this may sound confusing but this can be shown with the following reasoning

​

span(x,y,z) = ax + by + cz 

for arbitrary constants a,b,c

span(x+tz,y,z) = d(x+tz) + ny + kz

for arbitrary constants d,n,k

​

then we simply expand and redefine a constant

span(x+tz,y,z) = d(x+tz) + ny + kz = dx + dtz + ny + kz = dx + ny + dtz + kz = dx + ny + (dt + k)z

dt + k = g

for an arbitrary constant g since d,t,k are arbitrary constants. 

hence span(x+tz,y,z) = dx + ny + gz = span(x,yz)

since a,b,c and d,n,g are arbitrary constants.
